title: Tiered reservation mirroring and latency attenuation proxy
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: Dedicated customers occasionally see headroom oscillation when multiple reservation classes compete for burst capacity. This manifests as transient latency spikes during mid-burst when warm pools are being rebalanced. Motivation: introduce a reservation mirroring layer that periodically reflects committed reservation ratios into a lightweight read-only projection used by autoscalers and a latency attenuation proxy that applies short-term conservative backpressure during mid-burst churn. Design summary: 1) Tiered reservation mirroring component produces a compact view of per-tenant committed vs. available reservation fractions (hot/warm/cold tiers). The mirror is updated on reservation change events and decays gracefully when failures prevent updates. 2) Latency attenuation proxy sits in the request admission path for Dedicated pools; when the mirror reports rapid reservation churn or high variance in warm-pool occupancy the proxy enforces a short-duration soft throttle and prefers slower acceptance paths (defer-to-warm) to prevent KV-cache thrashing. 3) Telemetry normalizer: new aggregator exports smoothed percentile utilization and a mirrored_reservation_delta metric to help SREs detect misalignment between committed capacity and applied allocation. Backwards compatibility: mirror is read-only to existing allocators; feature is gated behind an opt-in policy flag per-pool to allow progressive rollout. Rollout plan: start with a canary in staging, run e2e reservation_mirror_test, enable for 2 low-traffic Dedicated pools for 48h with extra tracing. If no regressions promote to 20% of pools, then global. Safety: soft throttle only reduces peak admission by a bounded factor and preserves commit contracts; pessimistic by default and configurable via release flags. See docs/designs/tiered-reservation-mirroring.md for algorithmic details. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4123) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration + e2e tests - [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts stubs - [x] Feature gate and rollback path included

review_comments: Noah Simmons: Nice isolation of the mirror projection. Two requests: (1) add a small bounded queue to avoid N^2 updates when a tenant flips reservations repeatedly, (2) make decay time configurable via pool config (not a global const).
Priya Kapoor: Responding: added bounded coalescing queue with a default of 50 revisions and exposed decay_ms per-pool; updated docs to call out tradeoffs.
Elena Garcia: Can you justify the soft-throttle multiplier? In my local runs it seemed conservative but we need numbers for SRE runbooks.

Priya Kapoor: Added a short section in the design doc with the tuned multipliers (0.7 for mid-burst, 0.9 for low-variance) and included a knob for percentage reduction. Also added telemetry to emit the applied multiplier per-decision for post-mortem.
Markus Li: Found a potential deadlock in the mirror update path when DB writes fail; request a fallback that marks pool as 'mirror-degraded' rather than blocking updates.
Priya Kapoor: Implemented mirror-degraded path; autoscaler will fallback to last-known projection and emit mirror_degraded event. Added unit test to ensure no blocking behavior.

release_notes: - Added tiered reservation mirroring to produce read-only reservation projections for autoscalers. - Added latency attenuation proxy to reduce mid-burst latency spikes by applying short-duration soft throttles when reservation churn is detected. - Exposed per-pool decay and throttle knobs behind a feature gate for staged rollout.
